The consent state set, the verification rule, the failed-count threshold and the decision code of a consent change are parameters and reference data read with the version in force, and their values are left to the compliance and PDPA officer.

The retention class list, the class per document type and the periods are P5 rwb-document reference data and stay unset for this key (NFR-028, DL26). This story needs only the presence or the absence of a class per notice document, so a class value is carried through the coverage read as the owner returns it and is never validated, mapped, defaulted or stored here; when P5 publishes the list the coverage read carries the code and no rule of this story changes.

The central chain is built by recomputing entry_hash on the legacy canonical form (BR4) over the stored columns, appending under one advisory lock in ingest commit order, and keeping the local chain sequence and hash on the row for reconciliation.
decision_log_entry keeps every entry with no purge, no archive and no truncation in this story, and the retention period is read as a parameter when Compliance publishes it.
The audit read returns the masked value of the free-text fields under the policy of rwb-access in force, offers no unmasking operation, and the export carries the same masking as the screen.
REQ-ACA-006 and NFR-042 are read as covering the case store, the document store and the reporting read model, and the legacy lake analysis is retired with no target path.

For D7.1 the limit that applies on the screen is read as no amount limit at approval level none, shown as the approval level and the route role, and the DoA table is not consulted for this decision; the DoA table stays P4 rwb-access' and is read by the routing story where an amount-bearing decision uses it.

No data-lake element exists in this key: INT-19, INT-20 and the daily decision-log copy are retired, the record is published on rwb.decision-record.v1 and reporting reads events, and JOB-13 is continuous Kafka ingest in the owning service.

Every field of the two panels declares a mask flag of NONE, PARTIAL or FULL with a policy key; the postal address is PARTIAL, identifiers and codes are NONE, and the mask itself is applied by the route with the policy of rwb-access.

The shape of the contact entry and of its two reads is read as follows and is written in the story as a placeholder, never as a guess: the entry carries entryId, chainSeq, caseId, decisionCode, finalCall, ruleId, ruleVersion, inputsRef, an actions object holding the channel, the reason code and the requesting role, decidedAt, prevHash, entryHash, correctsEntryId and actorUserId, with no reason column of its own; the DecisionLogEntry answer carries the same fields and the DecisionLogPage answer carries items, page, size and total and is filterable by caseId with the from and to dates of TSD P7 v2 T-A.2; the inputs reference keeps the shape inputs/<businessDate>/<hash> of FSD P7 v3 AC-ALT-P7-001-02; and the search index of the case-and-date read is not named.

The refusal vocabulary of the contact check is read as follows: decision code X6 with final call contact refused covers all five causes of a refusal, and the cause is carried in the reason code as X6 Lost contact, X1 Dispute or complaint, No consent on the channel, Legal hold or Template withdrawn, the first two copied from the legacy message placeholder and the last three from the legacy scenario titles; the rule id of the entry is R-UNI-04 for a contact stop (with R-UNI-05 and R-DEV-16 as its supporting rules of BR2 and BR3, named in the rules rather than in rule_id), R-UNI-10 for no consent, R-UNI-20 for a legal hold and R-LIT-03 for a withdrawn template; a send that passed the check is appended with no reason code and with a final call that no source names, so the story carries it as a placeholder.

The shape of the field-capture decision entry and of its two reads is read as follows and is written in the story as a placeholder, never as a guess: the entry carries entryId, chainSeq, caseId, decisionCode, ruleId, ruleVersion, inputsRef, a recommendation holding the document type, the capture kind and the item result, finalCall, an object reference holding the document ID of a stored capture or the client file ID of a refused item, the client file ID, the document type code, the capture kind, the capture time, the message id of a refusal, decidedAt, prevHash, entryHash, correctsEntryId and actorUserId, as new columns of decision_log_entry; the DecisionLogPage answer carries items, page, size and total and is filterable by the object reference as well as by the eight query values of TSD P7 v2 T-A.2; the final call values are ACCEPTED, REFUSED and QUARANTINED, taken from the item result of the legacy field-capture response; MSG-P7-009 names ruleVersion or decisionCode and MSG-GEN-006 names the system that is unavailable; and the decision-log view of a case is described without a panel id.

The extraction decision entry carries, beside the TSD P7 v2 T3.1 columns of decision_log_entry, the document reference and version, the document type code, the field name, the field pattern or rule identifier and version, the parameter version in force, the confidence, the threshold value and the threshold reading; the final call is 'accepted' or 'sent to the review queue' as the work package fixes it; the decision code is a value of the list in force for the document decision and no new code is invented; the read answers the seven field groups of FSD P7 v3 AC-ALT-P7-001-02 plus the extraction facts, filtered by case and by the document reference the entry carries; and the panel id, the message ids of the extraction refusals and a feature switch of this capability are left unspecified until the design-time agreement of CG-B-P7-03-E2025-1.

The generation entry carries, beside the TSD P7 v2 T3.1 columns of decision_log_entry, the template codes with their versions, the treatment reference and the requesting role as members of actions, and the merge snapshot reference in inputs_ref; the version evidence the FSD asks of every record (a rule, a model or an agent version) is the template code and version pair of this record; the decision code is D6.4 and the final call is GENERATED as the work package fixes them; a record that names no template code with its version is refused; and the container names, the member names and the snapshot shape are left as written here until the design-time agreement of CG-B-P7-03-E2026-1.

The decision code of a reference-case step is read from the LOV-DECISION list in force and is never fixed by this story: the ledger stores the code the fact carries after validating it against the list, an unknown code is refused, and the reference-data fake supplies the route code the reference package uses, so no literal decision code appears in the story, the code, a test or a migration.

The chain-check outcome is read as follows: a complete run records the count, the last chain_seq, that entry's entry_hash, the start time and the end time in the service operational report and reports no break; a break is reported the same day to Compliance and RW-AUDIT as one notification naming the case, the chain_seq and the entry_hash of the entry before it, and the check writes no decision_log_entry row of its own, because a check is not a decision of a case. The completeness gap of a late fact is reported the same way, with the case, the key and the age.

The write-once daily seal of the ledger hash and the strict-mode acknowledgement before a point of no return are outside this story: the seal is read as a separate step of rwb-decision over this ledger with no story of RWB-E2-043, and strict mode is read as the points of no return of S4, S5, S6 and S7 reading a confirmation the ledger exposes, neither of which this story builds. The ADR-009 change Arch v5 slide 28 proposes needs Risk and Internal Audit sign-off, and that sign-off is an approval outside this run.

One escalation is read as two ledger entries and not as one. rwb-writeoff writes the local record of R-WO-12 with the state change and publishes it on rwb.decision-record.v1, and rwb-decision writes the routing record of the approval it raises; both are collected into the central ledger, each names the same case and the same rule and neither repeats the other's facts, and the ledger read returns them in chain order so the pair reads as one step. The same reading applies to R-WO-32 and the sale selection.

The accounting entry set, the chart-of-accounts reference and the posting type a match value maps to stay with the ledger and with Finance, and this service posts the facts of the matched receipt — case, proceeds, receipt, amount, value date, match value and route — as one item on the ledger interface; the mapping is held as data of the interface configuration and no account, cost centre or amount rule is written in code.

The built provision-input set is the answer of the build step: no table, no column and no event is created for it, and it is neither staged in rwb_payment nor delivered to Finance by this story; the finance provision feed, its file layout, its interface number, its transport, its retry policy and its acknowledgement stay out of scope until an interface is published, while the month-end close window of R-WO-26 is read as a policy timer of the write-off route and not as a Schedule of this service.

The case-side recompute of the segment, the route reopen and the hard-gate re-run of rules R-UNI-22 and R-UNI-37 stay with rwb-case, and rwb-reporting keeps only the reported classification and the record that names the rule version; the two services are joined by the case and rule events and by no shared table.

The limit the appraisal age is compared with is read as reference data or as a rule row with its version, and no S1 rule id is asserted: the decision record carries the rule id and the version in force on the business date where the source provides one, and otherwise the limit's version with the appraisal number, the age and the outcome, so that AC2 stays provable without inventing an S1 rule id.

The previous value is the latest prior appraisal of the same asset_key on the rwb-source-data data product, taken by appraisal date, and the basis used and its date are recorded on every check. If the business owner prefers the last accepted value of valuation_ext, the change is one read and the recorded basis, and the shape of the answer and the record does not change.

The gap that counts as an outlier, its unit and the rule that settles it are taken as one versioned reference-data row of rwb-case (default ruling of Template and Rules v1 §R3: parameters and reference data belong to P3 rwb-case) or as a row of the S1 rule package read through rwb-decision, with their valid-from date and their version; the step reads whichever is in force on the business date and flags nothing, recording the rule gap, where neither can be resolved. No percentage, distance, limit or appraisal type is written in code, as a default or as a branch of the build.

The band is read as a value in force with its version, carried on the rule-in-force or reference answer that its owner publishes, and the decision record stores the band with that version; no band identifier, boundary, floor or default is asserted, compiled or enumerated by this story or by its contract baseline, because the band policy is administered under FEAT-ADM-04 and no source publishes its values.

The rule id, the rule version and the route set are read from rwb-decision for the business date and recorded with the answer, and no S1 rule id, route set or threshold is asserted: where a source provides a rule row the record carries its id and version, and otherwise it carries the version in force with the per-route answer and the fallback flags, so that AC1 stays provable without inventing a rule.

The balances of the payoff are the ALS balances ACE holds, read at the ACE batch date through the rwb-source-data account data product or this service's own SELECT-only view of v_ace_account; total_balance, past_due_amount and collections_fee are the three elements AC1 names, and the composition of the payoff, the treatment of the collections fee and the rounding are governed values read with a version and never written in code.

The freshness limit of payoff_as_at, the range bounds, the floor method and the missing-value names are values of the settlement route set in force, read with the rule id and the rule version; both stories declare no numeric value for them and treat a change as a rule release.

The route-decision figures are read as data in force with their version and no rule id, decision code, confidence threshold, ranking weight or open-route exclusion is asserted: the open route set comes from the case and the rules in force, R-RES-32 is the one published exclusion, and the decision record carries the rule id and version in force on the business date where a source provides one, otherwise the version of the data used, so that AC1 stays provable without inventing an S1 rule id.

The recommended route is carried as a code of LOV-ROUTE and its name is read from the reference-data list in force; this story asserts no mapping of R4 to R8 onto the guarantee claim, litigation, asset sale, debt sale and write-off routes, and no mapping of any code is written in code or in a test fixture as a business rule.

The delegation-of-authority limit is a governed data row with a version, read for the caller's role from the authority matrix through rwb-decision. The step compares the chosen route with that limit, records the limit applied and its version in the decision record, and asserts no boundary: the limit value, its boundaries and the matrix row stay open as CG-B2-S1-008-1 until their owner publishes them, and the contract declares the element with its source and no value.

No S1 rule package is in force for the approval. The step reads whatever rule id and rule version the rwb-decision answer carries for the business date, records them with the limit applied, and applies no local decision table of its own; if the answer carries no rule id, the record carries the placeholder and the version of the decision answer, never an invented rule id.

The decision record carries the decision code D6 with the delegation version, the level applied, the final call and the coded reason, and it carries a rule id with its version only where the decision owner provides one; no S1 route-decision rule id is asserted, because no such row is published and the S1 package is not in force.

The branch declares two rights of the capability area Treatment and offer: right U for the four officer roles of the legacy permission table, who submit and read, and right RA for RW-CREDCOMM and RW-PRODHEAD per TSD S1 T6.1, who answer the escalated route. The legacy table is not widened by invention and the committee right is recorded as a conflict to be confirmed by the access matrix.

The rule id, the rule version, the segment dimensions and the gate thresholds are read from rwb-decision for the business date and recorded with the reopen, and no S1 rule id, threshold or parameter is asserted: where a source provides a rule row the record carries its id and version, and otherwise it carries the version in force, so that AC1 stays provable without inventing a rule.

The value trigger of the reopen is the appraisal value the case owner accepts in FEAT-VAL-04, read with its type and date on the rwb-source-data data product; the step treats it as one of the three kinds of new information and reports the reopen to the route decision, which then runs the expected return (FEAT-VAL-05) and the recommendation (FEAT-VAL-07) again, so this step claims neither feature's behaviour and no new value reopens on its own before the recompute.

The task set and the timer set of a route are governed rows with a version, read for the approved route through rwb-decision. The step composes the to state, the task codes and the timer types and values from that row, records them with the version applied, and asserts no code, no duration and no default: the sets, their codes and their values stay open as CG-B2-S1-012-1 until their owner publishes them, and the contract declares the elements with their source and no value. The element set of the route-start answer inside Approval is declared from the requirements (REQ-S1-007) and carries the placeholder where the source is silent.

No S1 rule package is in force for the route-start step. The step reads whatever rule id and rule version the rwb-decision answer carries for the business date and the approved route, applies that row's action, to state and timer, and applies no local decision table of its own; if the answer carries no rule id, the record carries the placeholder and the version of the decision answer, never an invented rule id.

The range the officer may move within is an amount band with the floor applied: settlementRangeLow and settlementRangeHigh from reference data, floorPrice below which R-SET-05 sends the offer to the approver, and the model installment and the count as the installment figures. No installment range is published as a separate field.

One activity serves both subrogation rows: R-GUA-23 from CLAIM_PAID and R-GUA-24 from CLAIM_PART_PAID set the same position with the same action and the same to-state, the claim record's status moves to PAID under LOV-CLAIM-STATUS in the same transaction, and the case states CLAIM_PAID, CLAIM_PART_PAID and SUBROGATION_POSITION are reported to the parent CaseWorkflow as the rows of the GUARANTEE state set.

The TCG share, its basis and its effective scope are governed values entered or confirmed on the claim update under right U of Treatment and offer, and no TCG interface is called, because INT-29 is recorded as not available today; the share is never a constant, a percentage or a default of the build.

The subrogation position of a closed guarantee is carried by the GuaranteeClose element recorded against the claim, with the guaranteed share and the balance after it; the state SUBROGATION_POSITION itself is entered by R-GUA-23 and R-GUA-24 and belongs to the sibling story RWB-S3-E4016-APP. No position entity, no position table and no position column is created by this legacy key until the data owner publishes its identifiers.

The proof window of 7 days and the notice period are two durable timers of LitigationWorkflow: the first starts at dispatch, the second at delivered_at under R-LIT-07 and never under R-LIT-08 or R-LIT-09. The notice period is a versioned reference row per product and notice type whose content is not published; when the row is missing the step records the decision, holds the timer and answers no move. The case-stage timer and the officer task stay rwb-case's rows, requested on the stage outcome.

The partner clock is one durable timer of LitigationWorkflow of 2 working days started at instructed_at on a working-day calendar read as a versioned reference row; on expiry R-LIT-28 fires, the instruction is marked breached on the partner contract, FIRM_BREACHED_SLA is answered to rwb-case with the partner-and-agency-manager task and the re-selection stays with the firm-selection story. The case-stage timer and the task row stay rwb-case's, requested on the stage outcome.

The accrued fee, the spend deadline, the value date and the approval state are read on rwb-payment's contract and are never written here. rwb-litigation owns no fee table and no fee column: its only durable effects are the hearing row, the decision record, the workflow timers and the stage answer, and the approved fee is posted by P8.

The proposal is not a business row. It is a view of the local decision record answered on API-S4-003 GET /legal-actions/{legalActionId}, with the proposed step, the reasons (rule ID, condition and facts), the cost and effect with its source, the deciding role and the package version. The step vocabulary is a versioned reference value whose content is not published, and the cost and effect are read on rwb-agent's contract under DP-20 with the rule as fallback. No sixth REST operation is added to the five of TSD S4 T-A.1 and `legal_action` gains no column.

The template status of R-LIT-04 is read on rwb-comms' notice contract as part of the notice answer, and the pack index of R-LIT-16 is read on rwb-document's contract with its defect list items. Both elements and both operation names carry the placeholder. When one of the two facts is absent the rule does not fire, nothing is written, no move is answered and the case keeps its state.

The appeal window length and the filing deadline of R-LIT-47 are versioned reference rows read with their version in force, held as durable timers of LitigationWorkflow, and their content is carried as the placeholder in both stories. No value is written in code and no figure is taken from another module's clock.

The approved court fee or legal expense is paid and posted against the case by rwb-payment (P8) and is never written in rwb_litigation: this service checks the fee against the schedule, routes it to the approver, writes one decision record per outcome and stores the payment reference the owner returns. No fee column, fee table, posting, ledger entry or balance exists here.

The fee schedule, the fee types and the court levels are versioned reference data of rwb-case, read on its contract; the schedule version is carried on every decision record; no schedule value, fee type or court level is a constant of the code, and DP-06 and DP-07 stay outside this key's pattern set with their dependency rows unclaimed.

The approval is the P7 rwb-decision child workflow named in TSD S4 T5.2.2 on queue rwb-decision, the D7.4 limit and the approver's delegation limit are read on the rwb-access authorise contract, and the LITIGATION package with R-LIT-30 and R-LIT-41 to R-LIT-43 is read from rwb-decision at its version in force. None of the three is rebuilt here, no limit value is fixed in code or in the document, and the H, C and I metadata rows stay exactly as the plan gives them.

Both stories carry Status Draft (realignment v1) and the missing approval of the realigned stories and of the FSD S4 and the TSD S4 they read is treated as an assumption of this run rather than as a blocker; no behaviour and no value of either story depends on a signature, and no status of a source document is changed.

The writ deadline of R-LIT-54 is one durable timer of LitigationWorkflow armed from a versioned reference value at its version; the reference value is Not specified in the source documents (CG-B2-S4-018-5; ASM-B2-S4-018-5), and no timer row, no Temporal Schedule and no Quartz row is created.
The Land Office registration is kept outside every service and is read as the registered transfer fact of RWB-S2-E3012-CON and as an officer step.

The holding age is derived from the asset dates the dictionary gives (stock_date, DF-COL-040, and transfer_in_date, DF-COL-036) and held as a durable timer of AssetDisposalWorkflow; the next provision step date is a reference value read at its version and held as the timer's end; no column is added for the age, the next step date or the cost to date beyond the columns the DB story of S5 publishes.

The rwb-source-data data-product read, the rwb-case state read and the rwb-case case-move answer are treated as class C dependencies even though the contract-dependency row of both slices is None: both stories build against the published documents of their owners and their fakes on Day 1, and the metadata rows keep the values the plan gives them.

Both stories carry Status Draft (realignment v1) and the missing approval of the realigned stories, of the legacy master and of the FSD S5 and TSD S5 files (which are absent from the extract set) is treated as an assumption of this run rather than as a blocker; no behaviour and no value of either story depends on a signature, and no status of a source document is changed.

The price model and the reserve basis are the pricing agent own and are read from its answer as a model reference with its version; this service stores the reference in the decision record, computes no proposal and fixes no reserve basis.

Both stories carry Status Draft (realignment v1) and the missing approval of the realigned stories and of the FSD S5, the TSD S5 and the Epics 3 to 8 Specification they read is treated as an assumption of this run rather than as a blocker; no behaviour and no value of either story depends on a signature and no status of a source document is changed.

The Land Office stays a person and officer step outside every service: the officer records the registration on the case task, it enters the service as the TITLE_REGISTERED signal of AssetDisposalWorkflow, and no interface, file, operation or X row is declared for it.
R-DIS-53, the rejected transfer and its TITLE_BLOCKED state, is out of scope of both slices until a story owns it; no criterion, message or task is invented for it now.
Both stories stand at Status Draft (realignment v1) and the missing approvals of FSD S5 v3, TSD S5 v2 and the Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 are recorded rather than waited for.

The tax criteria are a versioned fact in force read with the WO rule package from rwb-decision (P7), and tax_criteria_version is recorded with every outcome; the value is never a constant, a default or a branch of the code. An absent version holds the scan under R-WO-03 with MSG-S7-001 and writes nothing.

The TRANSFER package is read at its version in force, TRF-2026.11 or later, and its DEV trigger rows and row order are data of rwb-decision. The tests use the rule IDs and queues the legacy story publishes (TRF-001 to TRF-009 and the named queues) as package data, and no row, row order or target queue is written in code. The text of R-DEV-04 to R-DEV-06 is stated as a placeholder in the rule table until the rule owner publishes it.

The conditions, actions and target owners of R-DEV-04 to R-DEV-06 come from the Business Rules and Routing Logic workbook at build time, and the SCR-05 deviation fragment is rendered as a table of code, handler, paused state, contact stop and rule ID, with the refusal message beneath it and the cleared row shown as history.

LOV-TRANSFER-REASON carries R01 Capacity, R02 Customer deceased, R03 Skill, R04 Owner absent, R05 Legal referral and R06 Wrong queue as the intended set pending DL23, read at its version on the rwb-case reference-data contract and never written in code.
